newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.S. delegation seeks help for Kashmir hostages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. delegation seeks help for Kashmir hostages.

text.p: U.S. officials asked leaders of Pakistani-controlled Azad (free) Kashmir on Tuesday to help obtain the release of four Western tourists kidnapped in the Indian-held part of Kashmir in July 1995.

Ronald Mazer, regional security chief in the U.S. State Department, and other U.S. officials met Ishaque Zafar, acting prime minister of Azad Kashmir, officials in the Azad Kashmir capital Muzaffarabad said.

After the meeting, Zafar appealed for the release on humanitarian grounds of Britons Paul Wells and Keith Mangan, German Dirk Hasert and American Donald Hutchings, thought to be held by the shadowy al-Faran group of Kashmiri militants.
"The captives have no connection with the people related to the freedom struggle in Indian-held Kashmir," Zafar told the U.S. delegation.
"We firmly believe the abductions have been made at the behest of an Indian (intelligence) agency as the offence is serving only Indian interests," he added.
The U.S. delegation produced sketches of the suspected kidnappers. Zafar responded that the kidnapping could not be the work of Moslems.
U.S. diplomats in Islamabad could not immediately be reached for comment.
Pakistan controls one-third of Kashmir and India the rest of the disputed Himalayan region. A separatist insurgency against Indian rule has cost an estimated 20,000 lives since 1990.
